title: Logical Resource Estimation for Quantum State Preparation with Compilation
summary: Quantum state preparation is a fundamental primitive in quantum algorithms for encoding classical data into quantum amplitudes. We compare the cost of preparing general $n$-qubit states with real amplitudes using two common paradigms: rotation-based methods, based on controlled rotations, and sampling-based methods, based on a structured representation of the target state. Although these approaches are often theoretically compared using CNOT count and $T$-count, their relative performance in total gate count remains less well understood practically.
